title: Israel’s Soft Power Is Its Hard Power
gist: Anchal Vohra argues Israel is converting air-defense exports into diplomatic immunity: a $3.5 billion Greece deal for David's Sling, Barak MX and radars, Iron Dome and Iron Beam deployed to a UAE hit by 500+ Iranian ballistic missiles and 2,000 drones, and deep Indian co-production — all while the U.S. has burned through half its Patriot and THAAD stocks.

insights.claim: Israel's $3.5 billion defense deal with Greece covers David's Sling with a range up to 186 miles, the Barak MX system and air surveillance radars, building an integrated multilayered network against fighter aircraft, armed drones, cruise missiles, ballistic missiles and precision-guided weapons.
insights.speaker: Anchal Vohra
insights.so_what: A concrete, sized European order for Israeli air defense — evidence that NATO members are buying outside the U.S./European supply chain when capacity is constrained.
insights.locator: Under the deal, Israel will offer Greece

insights.claim: Israeli strategists explicitly believe recipient countries' dependence on Israeli defense kit is so great that they can hardly be expected to criticize Israel in diplomatic forums — arms sales are being run as a diplomatic-immunity strategy.
insights.speaker: Anchal Vohra
insights.so_what: Defense export dependency is measurably buying diplomatic cover — a reusable model for how mid-sized arms exporters convert industrial capability into political insulation.
insights.quote: these nations’ need for Israeli defense kit is so grave and their dependence on Israel so great that they can hardly be expected to criticize the country in diplomatic forums
insights.locator: Israeli strategists believe that with or without IMEC

insights.claim: Israel offers its key technologies only to partners it can trust, per retired brigadier general Sasson Haddad, meaning access to top-tier Israeli systems functions as a political loyalty test rather than a commercial transaction.
insights.speaker: Anchal Vohra
insights.so_what: Tiered technology access creates switching costs and long-term alignment — the mechanism by which the customer base becomes a de facto alliance.
insights.quote: even if the war continues and negotiations with Palestinians aren’t very good
insights.locator: In a world mired in conflict

insights.claim: The Greece deal lands as Netanyahu fights for political survival against Gadi Eisenkot in preelection polling, letting him show voters Israel is gaining ground abroad even as it loses traditional bastions of support.
insights.speaker: Anchal Vohra
insights.so_what: Defense export announcements are being used as domestic political currency — expect more deal announcements timed to the Israeli electoral calendar.
insights.locator: The $3.5 billion deal with Greece is welcome news

themes.theme: U.S. interceptor depletion creates the opening

insights.claim: The United States has burned through half of its Patriot and THAAD missile stocks, making the UAE increasingly dependent on Israel rather than its supposed prime security provider.
insights.speaker: Anchal Vohra
insights.so_what: A 50% depletion of U.S. interceptor inventory is both a massive replenishment order book for U.S. primes and the reason allies are diversifying to non-U.S. suppliers.
insights.quote: the United States, supposedly its prime security provider, has burned through half of its Patriot and THAAD missile stocks
insights.locator: Abu Dhabi further beefed up Emirati defenses

insights.claim: The UAE has been the most heavily bombed country by Iran, absorbing more than 500 ballistic missiles and 2,000 drones, prompting Israel to transport Iron Dome batteries and send dozens of military officials to operate them.
insights.speaker: Anchal Vohra
insights.so_what: Quantifies the interceptor consumption rate in a modern missile war — the binding constraint on air defense is magazine depth, not launcher count.
insights.quote: The UAE has been the most heavily bombed country by Iran, with more than 500 ballistic missiles and 2,000 drones.
insights.locator: At the other end of Israel’s defense partnerships

insights.claim: The UAE has added Spectro, a lightweight surveillance system detecting Iranian drones at about 12 miles, and Iron Beam, Israel's laser system that melts short-range drones and rockets — a shift toward cheaper per-shot counter-drone defense.
insights.speaker: Anchal Vohra
insights.so_what: Directed-energy defense is now combat-deployed, not experimental — a validated technology category with a clear cost-per-intercept advantage over interceptors.
insights.locator: Abu Dhabi further beefed up Emirati defenses

insights.claim: Iran reportedly had plans to attack European countries if it didn't get a desired deal from the U.S., and Cyprus was the only European country hit by an Iranian drone, leaving Greece and Cyprus aware they are within Iranian missile range.
insights.speaker: Anchal Vohra
insights.so_what: Southern European air-defense demand is being driven by a live Iranian threat, not just Turkish tensions — broadening the addressable market for Israeli and European systems.
insights.locator: The defensive shield will also protect Southern European nations

insights.claim: Apprehension about Turkey's rise and defense-industry expansion is the shared glue across Israel's partners: Israel fears Turkish buildup in post-Assad Syria under Ahmad al-Sharaa, India sees Turkey as a Pakistan backer, and the UAE distrusts Erdogan's support for the Muslim Brotherhood.
insights.speaker: Anchal Vohra
insights.so_what: Turkey's defense-industrial rise is generating a counter-coalition that funds rival procurement — bullish for Israeli and Indian defense industry, and a geopolitical headwind for Turkish exports.

insights.claim: Greece and Turkey tensions are escalating operationally and economically — Greek F-16s were scrambled last month after a Turkish drone entered claimed Greek airspace, with tensions intensifying over potential Eastern Mediterranean gas reserves.
insights.speaker: Anchal Vohra
insights.so_what: Intra-NATO conflict risk over East Med gas is a live political-risk discount on Eastern Mediterranean hydrocarbon development.
insights.locator: For Greece, it is trickier to contain a fellow NATO member

insights.claim: Cypriot Defense Minister Vasilis Palmas openly said the Greece-Israel air defense network protects Cyprus from Turkey, saying explicitly that all three countries face a Turkish threat — while Greece avoided naming Turkey officially.
insights.speaker: Anchal Vohra
insights.so_what: A NATO member publicly naming another NATO member as the threat is a marker of alliance fracture with real procurement consequences.
insights.quote: To be clear and explicit, what we mean is that all three countries face a threat from Turkey
insights.locator: Greece did not bring up Turkey

insights.claim: Netanyahu's 'hexagon' concept names Israel, Cyprus, Greece, India plus unnamed Arab and African countries as an axis against both the radical Shiite axis (Iran and proxies) and an emerging radical Sunni axis he identifies as Qatar, Syria and Turkey.
insights.speaker: Anchal Vohra
insights.so_what: Israel now publicly classifies Qatar and Turkey — both U.S. partners — as adversaries, a realignment that complicates U.S. Middle East policy and regional deal flow.
insights.quote: The intention here is to create an axis of nations that see eye to eye on the reality, challenges, and goals against the radical axes
insights.locator: For decades, Israel has steadily approached countries

themes.theme: India co-production and the IMEC corridor

insights.claim: India's DRDO and Israel Aerospace Industries jointly produce the Barak 8 surface-to-air missile system, and Israeli reconnaissance equipment is deployed on both the Line of Control with Pakistan and the Line of Actual Control with China, embedded across the Indian Army, Air Force and Navy.
insights.speaker: Anchal Vohra
insights.so_what: Deep co-production means the India-Israel relationship is structurally sticky — sanctions or boycott pressure on Israel would directly degrade Indian military readiness.
insights.locator: Then there is perhaps the most expansive defense relationship

insights.claim: India deployed Israeli equipment in the May 2025 Operation Sindoor conflict with Pakistan and was satisfied with its performance, with Netanyahu saying Israeli equipment 'worked very well.'
insights.speaker: Anchal Vohra
insights.so_what: Combat validation in a real peer conflict is the strongest sales credential in defense exports — supports continued Indian and third-country orders.

insights.claim: The India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor would run from India to the UAE and through Israel to Greece, deliberately bypassing Turkey — but it is unclear whether Saudi Arabia remains on board or when it becomes reality.
insights.speaker: Anchal Vohra
insights.so_what: IMEC is a Turkey-bypass trade route whose viability hinges on Saudi participation — a binary watch item for Eastern Mediterranean logistics and port investment.
insights.locator: The alliance Israel wants is still elusive

insights.claim: Partner countries have decoupled commercial defense ties from Palestine policy — all condemned bloodshed in Gaza and also condemned Hamas, support a Palestinian state, and the UAE joined Egypt, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and Turkey in condemning West Bank settlement expansion while deepening Israeli defense ties.
insights.speaker: Anchal Vohra
insights.so_what: Diplomatic condemnation is not a leading indicator of commercial rupture — Israeli defense export revenue has proven insensitive to Gaza-related political pressure.
insights.locator: Israel’s growing defense partnerships are essentially telling
